notes: SHIP v1.14.417 - S0 OF THE SITE PROFILE ROOT: ACTIVE_SITE_PROFILE EXISTS, WITH THE IDENTITY SPLIT, AND GATES NOTHING. Stage 0 of 4. This ship RECORDS and REPORTS. It switches no consumer, changes no surface, and blocks no boot. That is the entire point: a later stage puts a GATE on startup, and a gate can lock an operator out of a working device in a cold aisle, so the migration that feeds it ships first, alone, and gets proven against real data before anything depends on it. IDENTITY IS TWO PEOPLE, NOT ONE (SHIP-TECH-FLOW v2 section 2, owner ruled governing 2026-08-08). siteLead is AUTHORITY - set at Site Setup, changed only in SITE/SYSTEM. currentOperator is the ACTOR - whoever is doing the work on this device right now. They are usually the same person and the model never assumes it, because the Event Log credits work to the actor and must never auto-credit the Site Lead. currentOperator is NOT a new field: the existing operator field already means who is on THIS device (v1.6.70, its own comment says so) and already feeds signedOffBy. Adding a second field for the same fact would be the duplicate state this ruling deletes, so operator IS currentOperator and PHANTOM_SITE.currentOperator() is the name that says so. This SUPERSEDES the earlier single-identity wording (name = configured Site Lead, role = Site Lead); the role field is removed, because under the split Site Lead is a named slot on the profile, not an attribute of a person. THE MODEL - THE PROFILE OWNS AND BINDS, IT DOES NOT EMBED. The architecture ruling says ACTIVE_SITE_PROFILE contains normalized topology, hosts and cables. Taken literally that is one serialized blob, and the stress harness already measured a 4000-host Master compressing to about 6.5MB against Safari 5MB origin quota - every profile write would rewrite all of it and hit the cliff. Owner confirmed the reading. So the root record holds identity plus ONE binding (activeMasterId), and the heavy data stays in its own key reached through that binding. SAME KEY, NOT A NEW ONE: this extends phantom_site_profile_v1, because a root profile living beside the old profile would be exactly the duplicate state this ruling exists to delete. Fields added: siteLead, id, createdAt, activeMasterId, masterFile, masterBoundAt, rootMigratedAt. The id exists because the Event Log binds every entry to it as siteProfileId, so it must exist before any event can be written. SCHEMA VERSION DELIBERATELY NOT BUMPED - siteProfile_load merges DEFAULTS under the stored record, so an older profile reports the new fields empty at any schemaVersion. Bumping would mean editing two save paths that hard-code 2, and if either were missed the value would flip between 2 and 3 on alternate saves. VALIDITY IS COMPUTED, NEVER TRUSTED FROM STORAGE. activeMasterId records what the profile was set up against; whether it still HOLDS is answered by comparing it to the live Master at the moment of asking. A stored boolean goes stale the first time a Master is replaced, and a stale stored valid is exactly how a gate locks out a good device or admits a broken one. Validity returns a LIST OF NAMED REASONS rather than a boolean, because invalid is not a sentence a technician can act on in an aisle. MIGRATION IS THE PART THAT PROTECTS THE OPERATOR. Without it, the later gate would send every existing device - including one with a confirmed profile, a loaded Master and live deployments - straight into SITE SETUP, because no root record existed yet. It fills only what is empty, is idempotent, and is read-modify-write so it cannot wipe a field it has no input for (the v1.14.347 fresh-literal trap). siteLead is SEEDED from the one name already on record rather than invented: under the old model that human WAS the Site Lead, so after the split the same person correctly occupies both slots, which is the common case. EVERY FILL IS GATED ON confirmedAt - a device that never finished setup comes out untouched, not one field, not even the profile id. A BUG CAUGHT IN REVIEW AND FIXED BEFORE SHIP: the id fill was initially unconditional, which would have built half a profile in front of the Site Setup flow that is supposed to build it. TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS ON RECORD. First: activeDeploymentId is NOT copied into the profile. The ruling lists deployment state, but duplicating that id creates a second writable source for which deployment is active - the precise split this ruling removes. The deployment store stays canonical and the profile binds by activeMasterId. Second: migration runs inside the Master boot-restore, so a device with a confirmed profile and NO Master does not get seeded. Harmless while nothing gates, and at the gate stage that device correctly belongs in setup anyway. DEVIATION LOGGED, NOT RESOLVED: the governing spec sequences SITE-PROFILE as workstream 2, gated behind PHASE-ENGINE. This is workstream-2 work landing first. It was authorised directly by the owner before the spec arrived, and it is inert scaffolding rather than UI, but the spec says each step gates the next - so it is recorded as a deviation in PHANTOM_CURRENT_STATE section 2 rather than argued away. TESTS: spec 10-site-profile-root.spec.js, 12 tests, all green. The ones that matter are not that migration fills fields: they are that it NEVER overwrites a value a human set, that a second run writes nothing at all, that an UNCONFIRMED device is left completely untouched, and that a second operator is credited to themselves and never to the Site Lead. Also pinned: a stored valid:true does not make an unbound profile valid; no-master, no-binding, match and mismatch are four distinct reported states; and S0 GATES NOTHING - a device with no profile at all still boots to the normal shell with its nav. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep - all enforced by the commit hook, which is now the ship gate of record (the four subagents named in the spec cannot load from this CWD and have never run). No RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. No UI surface changed. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: this ship has no visible surface. Confirm v1.14.417 after clearing the service-worker cache, then confirm the app opens exactly as before - same site, same Master, same deployments, nothing asking you to set anything up. In the console, PHANTOM_SITE.describe() should report your real site, siteLead and currentOperator both showing your name, and master binding match.
